posts.cooked:
Foote:

The situation exists where chairman can go into the trash before operative right?

Well, sorta.  We take the Chairman down before the Operative about half the time, and we just remove his cards from play entirely.  If they went into the trash, when his deck reshuffled you could get a full-health Chairman back in play on his frontside, which would make no sense.

 

Sefirit:

So what exactly do you do with the Operative when she gets sucker punched?  I mean if she doesn't flip, but is destroyed do you leave her out and just start ignoring the text on the card?  I assume you don't put her in the trash, but removing her from the game seems like it may be equally incorrect.  If you leave her in play I would think the text is still active similar to a card kept around by fixed point.

I have the most recent printing of Rook City, and The Operative says "when reduced to 0 hp or fewer, flip her cards."  Since there's no extra protection from Shrine of the Ennead or anything, we've been playing it exactly like if the Chairman was destroyed while the Operative was alive: remove the character cards from play entirely and keep going.

 

It's possible that it's an oversight, though.

Foote:

Yeah I understand why you would choose to do that, but understand that would be a house rule. Officially there is nothing that says remove the Chairman character card from play when it would be destroyed. So it would have to go into the trash.Think of it as the Operative, who is still alive, using the Lazarus tanks to revive Chairman yet again.

From the rulebook:

"Whenever a target is reduced to 0 or fewer HP, put it into the associated trash, except in the cases of hero character cards and villain character cards.  Unless stated otherwise, when a villain character card is reduced to 0 or fewer HP, the villain is destroyed and the players have won the game!"

 

So the Chairman is clearly not supposed to go into the trash, but the game isn't supposed to be over if the Operative is still up, either.  Since it's destroyed but can't go into the trash, removing it from play entirely seemed like the only rational way to do it.

The rules text, as Jimmy said, reads:

> Unless stated otherwise, when a villain character card is reduced to 0 or fewer HP, the villain is destroyed and the players have won the game!"

The Operative mearly states that you can't win the game*.  The question then becomes whether destroying the villian and winning the game is a single action, or two actions.  If it's one action, then the Operative would keep the Chairman in play at 0 health, probably with his rules text still active.  If it's two actions, then the Chairman would be destroyed, which (as per the definition of "destroyed") would put him in the villian trash.

 

* I think.  I don't have the cards with me.
